name: Château de la Négly Coteaux du Languedoc La Clape Porte du Ciel 2015
text:
## Château de la Négly Coteaux du Languedoc La Clape Porte du Ciel 2015

**The story.** Château de la Négly sits in the [Massif de la Clape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massif_de_la_Clape) ([see it from above](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Ch%C3%A2teau+de+la+N%C3%A9gly,+La+Clape,+Narbonne,+France&t=k)), a small [limestone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limestone) mountain on the [Mediterranean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea) coast between [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne) ([see it from above](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Narbonne,+Aude,+France&t=k)) and the sea, in the [Aude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude) department of [Occitania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occitania_%28administrative_region%29). The estate has had several names: in the 18th century it was called Ancely, in 1781 it became Nerly, and in 1807 La Négly, later gaining the title of château. Several families owned it before the Paux-Rosset family set it firmly on the road to quality. They changed how the vines were farmed, replanted the vineyard completely, swapping old workhorse grapes such as [Aramon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Aramon+grape&go=Go), [Terret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terret_noir) and white [Carignan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carignan) for [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah), [Grenache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenache) and [Mourvèdre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mourv%C3%A8dre), and replaced the harvesting machine with secateurs and small crates. With the consultant oenologist Claude Gros they completely rethought the winemaking, and in 2006 they bought the neighbouring Domaine de Boède with a third partner, Alain Wittner. Today Bastien Paux-Rosset runs the vineyards: about 75 hectares, 50 at La Négly on clay-limestone and 25 at [Boède](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Domaine+de+Bo%C3%A8de,+Narbonne,+France&t=k) on sandy silt and [sandstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandstone) ([Clos des Spiritueux](https://closdesspiritueux.com/22666-la-clape-chateau-la-negly---la-porte-du-ciel-2017.html)).

**The wine: La Porte du Ciel.** "The Gate of Heaven" is the estate's flagship. It comes mainly from two vineyards at the entrance to the domaine, planted in 1996 on very stony, sandy clay-limestone soils. After a gentle maceration, the wine ages for 24 months in new oak barrels. Picking and sorting this small cuvée alone takes more than three days ([Clos des Spiritueux, 2015](https://www.closdesspiritueux.com/18912-la-clape-chateau-la-negly---la-porte-du-ciel-2015.html)). The German merchant Lobenberg lists the 2015 as 100% Syrah at 15.5% alcohol ([Lobenberg](https://www.gute-weine.de/produkt/la-porte-du-ciel-jahrgang-2015-33470h)); a French merchant gives later vintages as 70% Syrah and 30% Grenache ([Clos des Spiritueux, 2017](https://closdesspiritueux.com/22666-la-clape-chateau-la-negly---la-porte-du-ciel-2017.html)), so the blend may vary by year.

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [Languedoc-Roussillon vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/languedoc-roussillon) says the 2015 harvest began on 7 August. The hot weather produced plentiful ripeness, and potential quality was "very promising at the top end". In La Clape, among the driest places in France with about 600 mm of rain a year and up to 3,000 hours of sun, that meant very ripe, powerful Syrah ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massif_de_la_Clape)).

**What the critics say for 2015.** As listed by [Lobenberg](https://www.gute-weine.de/produkt/la-porte-du-ciel-jahrgang-2015-33470h) (checked on its page):
- **[Jeb Dunnuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeb_Dunnuck): 97 to 99** (from barrel).
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 96 to 99** (from barrel).
- **Heiner Lobenberg: 96 to 97.** He found it shining black and almost opaque, with a very expressive nose once decanted (he insists on decanting): dense stewed plum, black and raspberry fruit that is almost liqueur-like yet salty and mineral, smoked bacon, coffee and violets. The palate is ultra-dense and creamy, with strong tannins. He gives a drinking window of 2020 to 2037.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 93.5** (from your CellarTracker list).

The French merchant's description adds cherry and cocoa with vanilla and blond tobacco on the nose, and a rich, dense, smooth palate of blackberry with perfectly ripe tannins and remarkable length ([Clos des Spiritueux](https://www.closdesspiritueux.com/18912-la-clape-chateau-la-negly---la-porte-du-ciel-2015.html)).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is eleven years old, in the middle of Lobenberg's window of 2020 to 2037. After two years in new oak and with 15.5% alcohol, a big Syrah like this needs time, and it should now be at a good stage: the oak absorbed and the dark fruit joined by smoky, meaty and spicy notes. Decant it 1 to 2 hours ahead, as Lobenberg insists, and serve it slightly cool.

**Serving.** Serve at about 16°C, a little below room temperature, so the alcohol doesn't dominate, and [decant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decantation) it well ahead. A large glass helps.

**Food.** This is a wine for rich, robust dishes. My picks: a grilled or slow-roasted leg of lamb with garlic and rosemary, beef [daube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daube), [cassoulet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassoulet), or [wild boar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_boar) stew. Strong cheeses work too. I'd avoid delicate fish and very spicy food.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the three stores on this site lists Porte du Ciel. In France, Clos des Spiritueux sold the 2015 at €110 a bottle, now sold out ([Clos des Spiritueux](https://www.closdesspiritueux.com/18912-la-clape-chateau-la-negly---la-porte-du-ciel-2015.html)). For a wine scored this highly, I think that is good value.

**From the history books**
- **An island once.** La Clape was an island until about the 14th century, when silt from the [Aude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aude) river joined it to the mainland. Phoenician sailors called it Lykia, and the Romans, who began growing vines there, called it Insula Laci for its many lakes ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massif_de_la_Clape)).
- **A port that lost its river.** [Narbonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne), at the foot of the massif and about 15 km from the sea, was a prosperous port city in Roman times and after. It declined from the 14th century, when the river Aude changed course, the same silting that joined La Clape to the mainland ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narbonne); [Massif de la Clape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massif_de_la_Clape)).
- **A wind feared by Romans.** The fierce local wind, the Cers, was already known to the Romans as Circius. [Pliny the Elder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pliny_the_Elder) wrote that no wind was stronger, and [Seneca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seneca_the_Younger) mentions a temple in Narbonne where people gave thanks for the healthy skies it brought ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massif_de_la_Clape)).
- **Ancely, Nerly, Négly.** The estate changed its name from Ancely to Nerly in 1781 and to La Négly in 1807. One of the estate's wines today is called L'Ancely, recalling the old name ([Clos des Spiritueux](https://closdesspiritueux.com/22666-la-clape-chateau-la-negly---la-porte-du-ciel-2017.html)).

**Curious details**
- **"Pile of pebbles".** The name La Clape comes from the Occitan word "clapas", meaning a rocky scree slope or pile of pebbles ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massif_de_la_Clape)).
- **A sinkhole with a sweet name.** In the massif lies the Gouffre de l'Œil Doux, a round [sinkhole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinkhole) about 64 metres across, filled with brackish water linked to the sea ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massif_de_la_Clape)).
- **Rare eagles.** Above the coastal town of [Gruissan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gruissan) ([see it from above](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Gruissan,+Aude,+France&t=k)) nests a pair of [Bonelli's eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonelli's_eagle), one of only about thirty in France (as of 2017), among garrigue, [kermes oaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quercus_coccifera) and [Aleppo pines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinus_halepensis) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massif_de_la_Clape)).
- **A radar on the hill.** The highest point, Pech Redon, is just 214 metres, yet since 1965 a French military radar station on the massif has watched over part of the western [Mediterranean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea).
